what: CRAN tests: never assert on timing
title: CLAUDE.md
text: Never put wall-clock timing expectation test can run CRAN: expect_lt()/expect_true() Sys.time() differences, system.time(), proc.time(), bench/microbenchmark results, elapsed-time threshold. CRAN check machines shared heavily loaded, elapsed time random timing assertion fails random. text: quoted string regex production (::=) contains | / now matched literally. production folded one regular expression, escape_string_for_regex() escaped ( ) [ ] - ^ * ? + \ | (alternation) / (trailing context), bars ::= '||'+; rejected ||||, slash ::= '/'+; rejected /, x ::= '|b'; matched b instead |b. Ported upstream jplevyak/dparser@51a4d04 (#43). Compiling grammar regex production (::=) whose quoted strings mostly regex metacharacters, x ::= '||||||||'; x ::= '++++++++';, longer overflows heap buffer (_FORTIFY_SOURCE aborted R session). convert_regex_production_one() sized combined regex unescaped string lengths, escaping can double (#43). mkdparse(rdebug = TRUE) longer overflows stack: debug grammar printer read version 30-byte buffer although d_version() writes 46 characters, d_version() measured uninitialised buffer. printer also longer leaks double-escaped copy string regex terminals (#40, jplevyak/dparser#34). Token locations now correct grammars large enough need 16- 32-bit scanner tables. scan_buffer() recorded token’s end line column consuming last character, positions – including syntax error positions – one column short, one line short token ending newline. Small grammars affected. Ported upstream DParser a1f64e7 (#44). regular expression bracket range ends \xff (example "[\x80-\xff]+") longer makes mkdparse() / dparse() loop forever building scanner. range counter build_regex_nfa() uint8 wrapped 255 back 0; now int (#42, upstream jplevyak/dparser 6d494a3). Generated parser tables longer contain raw bytes 0x80-0xff macOS. escape_string() used isprint(), macOS treats true bytes UTF-8 locale, grammar "[\x80-\xff]+" produced invalid UTF-8 C source dparse() failed gsub() “‘replacement’ invalid”; bytes now always written \xNN escapes (#42). regular expression term, * + loop inside one | alternative longer leaks sibling alternatives: "*|b" used also accept "ab" "aab". build_regex_nfa() now gives group level alternative start state (#42, upstream jplevyak/dparser 6d494a3). tables generated rxode2’s grammars unchanged. case-insensitive regular expression term ("..."/) now folds case inside bracket classes negating , "[^]"/longer matches "[-c]+"/matches aBc (#42, upstream jplevyak/dparser 6d494a3).

(fd <= 0) -> (fd < 0) fd 0 treated valid descriptor (stdin slot, returned open() stdin closed). d_pass(D_Parser*, D_ParseNode*, int pass_number) now rejects negative pass_number values explicitly. Previously bound check upper-(pass_number >= npasses), negative argument fell &p->t->passes[pass_number] subsequent pp->kind read landed passes[] array — typically SIGSEGV, occasionally silent garbage dispatch. fix adds matching lower bound; function now calls Rf_error("bad pass number: %d") negative argument. udparse() (therefore dparse() legacy wrapper) now returns NULL called NULL buffer. Previously NULL buf forwarded exhaustive_parse, scanner dereferenced (*s inside white_space) crashed. new guard top udparse short-circuits call state touched. new_D_Parser() now rejects negative sizeof_ParseNode_User. Previously negative argument stored verbatim, per- PNode allocation make_PNode uint l = sizeof(PNode) - sizeof(d_voidp) + sizeof_user_parse_node underflowed small value, rest make_PNode wrote past resulting tiny buffer. valgrind pre-fix build reported 281 invalid writes size 8, rooted make_PNode (parse.c:965). fix, new_D_Parser calls Rf_error clear message; valgrind reports 0 errors. dparse_sexp() (entry point used every per-grammar dparse_<gram>() wrapper) now reads input file buf_read() instead sbuf_read() + strlen(). Previously, callers cast strlen(buf) int, silently truncated wrong (often negative) value input exceeded INT_MAX bytes; negative length propagated p->end = buf + buf_len, making parser read random memory buffer.
